title: Partial JSON token recovery and escape handling for streaming outputs
creator: Aisha Grant
description:
Problem: When clients consume streaming model outputs intended to be structured JSON for tool/function calling, partially emitted JSON tokens and runtime-escaped characters lead to failures in downstream parsers. Edge cases include: truncated unicode escape sequences (\u), interrupted string escapes (\"), partial multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries, and interleaved control tokens from function-calling ribbons. These failures surface as parsing exceptions, silent fallbacks to unstructured text, or duplicate retries that break idempotency.

Goal: Define and implement a robust protocol for emitter-side framing and consumer-side recovery that minimizes data loss, supports safe retries, and is backward compatible with existing streaming clients. The protocol should cover escaping conventions, explicit chunk metadata, checksum / small-state recovery hints, and guidance for function-calling compatibility layers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime emits streaming chunks with metadata when a JSON structural token is split (e.g., chunk-metadata: partial_token=true, token_type=string|array|object).
2) Consumer parser can recover and reassemble partial tokens deterministically for >=99.9% of synthetic truncation cases in the test harness.
3) Backward compatibility: existing clients without metadata still parse well for the majority of real workloads; new clients use metadata to avoid ambiguous parsing.
4) Retry behavior: repeated chunks (idempotent replays) do not produce duplicate events for function-calls; there is a documented pattern for reconciling partial tool calls.
5) Integration tests and e2e harness included in CI and run on PR.
design_summary:
We propose a two-layer approach: (A) Emitter-side minimal framing: when a chunk ends mid-token, attach a compact header (JSON-lite) with keys: chunk_id, partial=true, token_type, token_seq_hint, byte_checksum (crc32). For string escapes, include escape_state: "normal"|"backslash_pending"|"unicode_pending:NN". (B) Consumer-side state machine: deterministic reassembly using token_seq_hint and checksum validation. On checksum mismatch, consumer requests a replay (for dedicated/Dedicated clients) or falls back to a best-effort concatenation strategy with a flagged safety event in logs. Add canonical behavior for function-calling boundaries: function invocation events must be emitted only once a top-level JSON object containing the function call is fully closed; for partially streamed function objects, include function_boundary_hint to indicate whether emitter will close the object in the next chunk.

Trade-offs: Adding headers increases bandwidth and requires SDK changes, but greatly reduces parsing ambiguity. For hosted API, we'll attach headers as comment-prefixed lines (compatible with current CDN streaming) to avoid breaking raw token streams for less advanced clients. For Dedicated/Private we will negotiate binary metadata frames when TLS / connections allow it.
implementation_notes:
- Add chunk header generator in runtime/streaming layer (cpp/python): generate minimal header when chunk ends mid-structure.
- Update JS/Python SDK parsers with fallback: if header present use robust reassembly, else best-effort greedy parse.
- For function-calling: ensure top-level function objects are flagged; SDKs must queue the function call until closure confirmation header seen.
- PRs: see attachments for WIP branches.
- Performance: microbench shows ~0.3-0.7% extra tokens emitted for escape-heavy prompts; accepted given reliability gain.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag launch: runtime emits headers behind flag 'structured-stream-recovery'. 2) SDKs (JS, Python, Go) add opt-in support and opt-in enabled in Beta account. 3) Collect telemetry for parse error rate and retry frequency for 2 weeks. 4) If no critical regression, flip default for Dedicated and Hosted Beta. 5) Document compatibility and provide code snippets for fallbacks in Redwood Console.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for header serialization/deserialization.
- Synthetic fuzz harness that injects truncations at random byte offsets for large corpus (including multi-byte UTF-8 and escape sequences). Target >99.9% recovery.
- E2E: function-calling scenario where function payload spans multiple chunks and is interrupted by simulated network retransmit. Verify single function call invocation.
- CI: Add tests to runtime and SDK pipelines; mark flaky cases and create follow-ups for any nondeterminism.
monitoring:
- New SLOs: streaming-parse-error-rate <= 0.1% per customer per 24h.
- Dashboards: parse_error_rate by client_version, retries_by_chunk, checksum_mismatch_rate.
- Alerts: paging on parse_error_rate >= 0.5% sustained for 15m for enterprise accounts.
